# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I see a display reading 0, the light is off, the plate is engraved with “?”, and there are three wires in order: red, yellow, blue. Blind’s pointing gesture may be intended to get my attention, but it conveys no actionable bomb instruction by itself.

```text
speak(text="The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved question mark. Wires from left to right are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👉]

Mute’s gesture clearly encodes three and right, but the exact intended operation is ambiguous: it may identify wire 3 or indicate a right-side action. I should ask Mute to clarify before Blind touches anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see three upward-pointing gestures followed by a right-pointing gesture. Do you mean wire 3, or a right-side operation? Please clarify the required action.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ 👉]

Mute has repeated the same gesture sequence, so I still cannot determine whether it means “wire 3” or something else. I should not authorize Blind to cut or manipulate anything based on that ambiguity. I will report the repeated signal and ask Mute for an unambiguous spoken instruction, though Mute may be unable to provide one.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again signalled three upward gestures followed by right. I cannot determine the intended operation; do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your signal remains ambiguous to me. Please send an explicit instruction in words if possible, including the wire number and action.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👉]

The new signal is shorter and clearer: 🤟 commonly represents three, followed by 👉 indicating right. This likely identifies the third wire or a rightward operation, but it still does not explicitly say whether to cut, connect, or move anything. I will relay the signal to Blind without inventing an action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now signals: three, then right. I see wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No explicit cut or connect instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute’s current signal is three upward gestures, most naturally indicating “three.” I should relay that this likely identifies the blue third wire, while avoiding any unsupported instruction to cut or manipulate it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals three. This likely identifies wire 3, the blue wire, but no action has been specified. Do not cut or alter it yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🫳]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s signal is three followed by a downward/open-hand gesture, while Blind has signalled “no.” The intended action remains uncertain, so I should not tell Blind to manipulate wire 3. I will relay both signals and ask Mute to provide a definite safe instruction through gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see three followed by a downward open hand. Blind has signalled no. Please clarify the exact action using an unambiguous gesture sequence.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals three, then a downward open hand. You signalled no. I do not have a confirmed action.")
wait()
```
